texts.preamble: Madhusudan vs Food And Drug Administration Dhar on 9 August, 2018 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Bench At Indore Writ Petition No.6416/2018 (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) -1- Indore, dated 09/08/2018
texts.facts: The petitioner No.4, M/s. Nestle India Limited is a Company registered under the Companies Act having its registered office at 100/101, World Trade Centre, Barakhamba Lane, New Delhi along with its nominee petitioner No.3 as well as Proprietors who are selling the food products manufactured by M/s. Nestle India Limited, are before this Court being aggrieved by orders dated 12/05/2016 and 04/10/2017 by which the adjudicating Officer has rejected the representation of the petitioners in respect of prosecution of the petitioner for violating the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 read with Regulation 2012 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011. 02- The petitioners' contention is that certain samples of Maggi Noodles were picked up from the shop of petitioner No.1 and the Food Safety Officer has submitted the sample for analysis to the Food Analyst, State Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal and the sample was subjected to examination. The samples were collected HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) on 29/05/2015 and a report was submitted on 22/12/2015. The report is on record and the same reflects that no MSG was added. In spite of the aforesaid, it was observed that sample has been misbranded. The sample was sent to the laboratory and the report of the laboratory also does not reveal the detection of any Mono-Sodium Glutamate (MSG). 07- In similar circumstances, in case of ITC Limited (supra), the ITC Limited was again being prosecuted for mentioning "NO MSG ADDED" and co-ordinate Bench of this Court has passed a detailed and exhaustive order in Writ Petition No.5427/2016. Paragraphs No.02 to 21 of the aforesaid judgment reads as under:- 2/ In brief, the petitioner's case is that it is engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing of various packaged products including 'noodles' and 'pasta' under the brand name 'Sunfeast'. The Food Safety Officer, Dewas had taken sample of 'Sunfeast Yippee Noodles Magic Masala' from retail premises of M/s Neelkamal Multi Trade Pvt. Ltd. on 1.6.2015 and had issued notice in Form VA under Rule 2.4.1 (3) of Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011 to the retailer only. The petitioner was issued notice by the Adjudicating Authority and the petitioner by appearing before the Adjudicating Authority had filed objection with respect to the maintainability of the complaint and prayed for dropping the proceedings on the ground that charge was not made out. By the order dated 26.7.2016 the Adjudicating Officer has rejected the objection and has held the complaint to be maintainable.
texts.arguments: 03- Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners has argued before this Court that only declaration, which is creating problem in his case is that the company has mentioned over the product that no MSG is added. He has vehemently argued before this Court that it was not at all established that the MSG was added and in those circumstances, the question of misbranding, as alleged, doesn't arise. He has prayed for quashment of impugned orders, which are subject matter of the present petition. He has also drawn the attention of this Court toward the judgment delivered in the case of ITC Limited Vs. State of M.P. & Others in Writ Petition No.5427/2016, which was also delivered by a co- Madhusudan vs Food And Drug Administration Dhar on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194655929/ 1 ordinate Bench of this Court in similar circumstances. 04- On the other hand, the learned Government Advocate has argued before this Court that by printing over the product that it does not contain MSG, the samples have been misbranded and as the samples have been misbranded, they have rightly initiated action against the petitioner under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 read with Regulation 2.12 of the Food HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011. 05- However, it has not been disputed by the learned Government Advocate that the report submitted by the laboratory does not reveal that any MSG was added by the manufacturer i.e. the petitioner company. A prayer has been made for dismissal of the writ petition. 06- Undisputedly, the petitioner before this Court has stated categorically over the food products manufactured by him that no MSG has been added by him. The sample was submitted for analysis to the Food HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) Analyst, State Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal and the report dated 4.7.2015 was obtained, in which no Monosodium Glutamate (MSG) was detected yet the Food Analyst in the reprot dated 22.12.2015 declared the samples to be misbranded on the ground that mentioning of 'No MSG Added' is misleading under Regulation 2.3(1)(5) of the Packaging and Labelling Regulation. The further case of the petitioner is that sanction for prosecution was wrongly granted by order dated 28.5.2016 by the designated officer and in pursuance to the said sanction the Food Safety Officer, Dewas had preferred a complaint before the Court of Additional District Magistrate-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Dewas alleging violation of Section 26(1),(2)(ii)(v), 3(zf)(A)(i), of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulation 2.3(1)(5) of the Packaging and Labelling Regulation and being liable under Section 27(1) of the Act and punishable Madhusudan vs Food And Drug Administration Dhar on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194655929/ 2 under Section 52 and Section 58 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. 3/ Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that since no MSG was detected in the laboratory test of the sample, therefore, it is not a case of misbranding. He further submits that the petitioner had neither added MSG nor its natural presence was found, therefore, prosecution cannot be sustained. He has also submitted that the sanction was granted by the concerned authority mechanically without application of mind. 4/ As against this, learned counsel for the respondents has supported the impugned action submitting that the petitioner had mentioned in the label that "No MSG Added" which was misleading since no negative declaration could be given and the petitioner could only mention the contents which were present on the label and could not have mentioned the contents which were not present. 6/ On the perusal of the record, it is noticed that the petitioner is sought to be prosecuted under the provisions of the Food, Safety and Standard Act, 2006 (for short "the Act") and the F.S. & S. (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 (for short "the Regulations") on the ground of misbranding the product namely 'Sunfeast Yippee Noodles Magic Masala'. The sample collected by the Food Safety Officer and analyzed by the Food Analyst was sent to the notified laboratory and its HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) report was obtained vide Annexure P/2. The report reveals that 'No MSG' was detected in the sample. In the reply also the respondents have admitted that as per the report of the Food Analyst MSG content was not found in the sample. The petitioner is being prosecuted only on the ground that printing of declaration 'No MSG Added' in the sample label was misleading under Regulation 2.3(1)(5) of the Regulations and it was misbranding under Section 3(ZF)(A)(i) of the Act. 9/ Section Madhusudan vs Food And Drug Administration Dhar on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194655929/ 3 3(zf) of the Act defines misbranded food and Section 3(zf)(A)(i) relevant for the present purpose reads as under:- Section 3(zf) "misbranded food" means an article of food- (A) if it is purported, or is presented to be, or is being- (i) offered or promoted for sale with false, misleading or deceptive claims either- (a) upon the label of the package, or (b) through advertisement; or 10/ For attracting this provision the label of the package of an article of food offerred for sale should have false, misleading or deceptive claim. Section 26(1)(2)(ii)(v) of the Act and the Regulation 2.3(1),(5) and Section 27(3)(c) and Section 27(2) (c) provides for the prosecution for misbranding of the product or substandard product or product containing extraneous matter or unsafe product but the only allegation against the petitioner is of misbranding of product. (See: 1992 Supp(1) SCC 335, State of Haryana and others Vs. Bhajanlal and others). When it is certain that there is no prospects of the case ending in conviction, the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on a future date and that when the trial is going to be nothing but a farce, such a course of action should not be allowed to take place. [See:(1996) 9 SCC 766, Satish Mehra Vs. Delhi Administration and Another]. 17/ In the matter of Pepsi Foods Ltd. and Another Vs. Special Judicial Magistrate and others reported in (1998) 5 SCC 749 wherein the petitioner was sought to be prosecuted on the complaint of selling adulterated beverages under the brand name of 'Lehar Pepsi' and had approached the court after receiving the summons , the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that:- "28. Summoning of an accused in a criminal case is a serious matter. Criminal law cannot be set into motion as a matter of course. The Magistrate has to carefully scrutinise the evidence brought on record and may even himself put questions to the complainant and his witnesses to elicit answers to find out the truthfulness of the allegations or HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) Madhusudan vs Food And Drug Administration Dhar on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194655929/ 7 - 10 - otherwise and then examine if any offence is prima facie committed by all or any of the accused. 29. [See: AIR 1997 SC 3400, Mansukhlal Vithaldas Chauhan Vs. State of Gujarat]. [See: AIR 1958 SC 124 Jaswant Singh Vs. State of Punjab]. [See: AIR 2014 SC 2369, P.L. Tatwal Vs. State of M.P.]. Sanction is a weapon to discourage vexatious prosecution and it is a safeguard for the innocent, though not a shield for the guilty. Consideration of the material implies application of mind, therefore, the order of sanction must ex facie disclose that the sanctioning authority had considered the HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE (Madhusudan Modi & Others Vs. State of M. P. & Others) - 11 - evidence and other material placed before it. [See: AIR 2014 SC 827, CBI Vs. Ashok Kumar Aggarwal].
